name: Mark Zuckerberg
role: Co-founder, chairman and CEO of Meta Platforms (Facebook) since 2004; co-founder of the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative and FWD.us
summary: Zuckerberg is a technology executive whose public positions centre on free expression, open technology and immigration. In 2017 he urged a more generous safety net, including exploring a universal basic income, higher contributions from the wealthy and openness to immigration and trade; in 2019 he defended broad free expression and political speech on platforms. In January 2025 he reversed Meta's fact-checking and moderation approach, citing government and media pressure, and he now favours a close working relationship with the Trump administration on AI and energy.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Said wealth inequality hurts everyone and that "people like me should pay for" a new social contract; reported to have funded the 2020 California ballot measure to tax commercial property at market value. He has not stated a specific tax rate position.

cut-welfare.rationale: Argued for a stronger safety net (a cushion, portable healthcare, affordable childcare) and a new social contract in the tradition of the New Deal and Great Society, the opposite of cutting welfare; he did not discuss welfare dependency directly.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Said American law does not recognize hate speech as a category and that the definition of dangerous speech should not expand beyond what is necessary (Georgetown 2019); his January 2025 policy changes removed Meta rules on topics like immigration and gender identity. He still supports platform rules against dehumanizing content and incitement, which are company policy rather than law.

rehabilitation.rationale: Called for a society that "focuses less on locking us up or stigmatizing us"; FWD.us, which he co-founded, also advocates criminal justice reform.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Joined Facebook employees marching in the 2013 San Francisco Pride parade after the Supreme Court struck down DOMA; no direct statement on marriage law found.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Co-founded FWD.us (2013), which lobbies for immigration reform, a path for undocumented immigrants and more skilled-worker visas, and criticized the January 2017 executive order limiting immigrants and refugees; in his 2017 Harvard speech he listed immigration among the flows to protect from those who would slow them down.

free-trade.rationale: In the 2017 Harvard speech he set "the flow of knowledge, trade and immigration" against those who would slow them down, while acknowledging people left behind by globalization; he did not claim everyone gains.

limit-growth.rationale: Wrote that AI and open source will "accelerate economic growth", and his Harvard speech asks for progress measured beyond GDP rather than for less growth; no statement on limiting growth for the environment.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Named stopping climate change as a candidate for generation-defining public works and said no country can fight it alone; this is a call for large collective projects, not a stated view on government mandates.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Wrote he is "extremely optimistic that superintelligence will help humanity accelerate our pace of progress" and urged public projects to cure diseases and fight climate change, while noting technology is eliminating many jobs and creating new safety risks.

experts-over-public.rationale: Said experts "have their own biases" and that he deferred too much to media and government critiques on moderation; also said he initially deferred to health authorities at the start of COVID. About information policy, not policymaking generally.

basic-income.rationale: Told Harvard graduates "we should explore ideas like universal basic income to give everyone a cushion to try new things"; an exploratory endorsement rather than a detailed program.

democracy-best.rationale: Argued that in a democracy people, not tech companies, should decide what is credible, and framed the central struggle as freedom and openness against authoritarianism; he did not address democracy when voters choose badly.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Argued that anyone taking initiative gets criticized for moving too fast, that the cost of inaction is ignored, and pushes to build frontier AI and open-source it; he also says risks need rigorous mitigation.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: His 2019 privacy vision made end-to-end encryption a principle ("prevents anyone, including us, from seeing what people share") and Meta rolled it out across messaging; he did not address government demands for access in the sources read.

positive-liberty.rationale: Argued that giving people "the freedom to pursue purpose" requires a financial cushion, childcare and portable healthcare, not only the absence of barriers.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Repeatedly framed inclusion as central: every generation "expands the circle of people we consider one of us", Muslims "always welcome" on Facebook, and equal voice for everyone.

party-controls-media.rationale: Opposes government control of information: said the Georgetown stand for free expression is needed against laws that undermine it, and in 2025 said the government telling platforms to "censor true things" was a disaster; Meta ended third-party fact-checking in 2025.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Pledged with Priscilla Chan to give away 99% of their Facebook shares through the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative and signed the Giving Pledge; told graduates that giving everyone freedom to pursue purpose "isn't free. People like me should pay for it."

notes: Living person: answers are recorded only where he or his organizations stated or acted on a position. His views on content moderation changed: in 2019 he defended platform rules against hate speech and misinformation, while in January 2025 he ended third-party fact-checking and loosened rules, saying the earlier approach had gone too far; the recent position is used. His 2017 progressive social-contract views (basic income, taxes on the wealthy) predate his later rapprochement with the Trump administration, and he has since said he leans toward neither party and wants a productive relationship with whoever governs; no 2025-26 statement reversing them was found. Nationalism versus global cooperation (nation-first) is left null because his 2017 global-community stance and his 2025 "American companies should win" AI stance are not directly comparable. The January 2025 post was written by Joel Kaplan; it is used as Meta policy Zuckerberg announced on video.
